summary.intent: Improve memory quality in the memory-loop system by enforcing evidence-based gating on generated memory records, and fix several UX issues in the summary command (slow startup, missing facets, broken repo filter).
summary.outcome: Implemented a two-layer evidence gate replacing the weak prompt-based filtering; fixed JSON parsing failures causing silent facet extraction errors; removed auto-backfill from summary command startup; corrected the repo branch filter to use git-reachability from default branch.

repo: memoryloop generator uses prompt instructions (not code) to enforce memory quality — a model suggestion, not a hard gate
passesReviewDerivedGate was the only per-kind evidence check; all other memory kinds had no multi-session enforcement
SourceSessionIDs is LLM-populated and unvalidated — cannot be trusted without cross-referencing against PatternAnalysis.AffectedSessions
improve/analyzer.go filtered out skill opportunities with count < 2 before the generator, making the singleton exception in the evidence gate unreachable
AffectedSessions uses checkpoint IDs while the prompt exposed session IDs — identifier mismatch would cause false rejections in Layer 2
summary_cmd.go ran backfill unconditionally on every invocation, causing 20+ sequential LLM calls with no progress output on first load
Personal-scope records become active immediately under auto-activation policy, bypassing TUI promotion entirely
The repo filter in summarytui used GetDefaultBranch (returning 'main') but sessions were on feature branches — always empty
Repo scope in memory-loop means checkpoints reachable from default branch HEAD via git history, not just branch name matching

LLM responses include trailing text after JSON (e.g. 'note:...') causing json.Unmarshal to fail with 'invalid character n after top-level value' — affected memoryloop generator, facets extractor, and improve generator

code.finding: Prompt instruction 'Avoid one-off incidents without repeated evidence' is a suggestion to the LLM, not enforced in code
Post-filter only catches low confidence/strength and generic advice; high-confidence singleton records pass through
SourceSessionIDs captured but never validated for length or accuracy
passesReviewDerivedGate enforced count>=2 only for review-derived rules, not other kinds — replaced by passesEvidenceGate
Skill opportunities with count < 2 dropped before generator sees them, making singleton exception unreachable — threshold lowered to 1
Both summaryBackfillSummaries and summaryBackfillFacets called unconditionally on every launch, writing to io.Discard with no progress
Detail pane checks row.HasFacets; after removing auto-backfill, this was always false until user pressed 'g'
ExtractJSONObject added as shared utility; previously each package would need its own copy

workflow: When the LLM returns JSON with trailing natural-language text, json.Unmarshal fails silently — errors were logged at DEBUG level only, not surfaced to users
Moving shared utilities (like ExtractJSONObject) to jsonutil prevents duplication across facets, memoryloop, and improve packages
Evidence gate design: Layer 1 checks provenance via source_signal.key against PatternAnalysis signals; Layer 2 validates SourceSessionIDs against both input.Sessions and signal.AffectedSessions
Singleton exceptions should be scoped by both signal kind AND record kind to prevent exception leakage across types

friction: passesReviewDerivedGate was the only existing enforcement pattern but only covered one record kind — had to generalize the pattern to all kinds
Identifier mismatch between AffectedSessions (checkpoint IDs) and prompt-exposed session IDs required switching the prompt to use checkpoint IDs
LLM trailing text after JSON caused silent failures in three separate packages; required adding ExtractJSONObject fallback everywhere
Multiple test files needed updating after removing defaultBranch parameter from newRootModel and RunWithCurrentBranch signatures
replace_all missed some newRootModel call sites because they had different parameter patterns (e.g. with generateFn argument)
After removing the repo filter, user clarified 'repo' means merged-to-main (git-reachable), not just 'all branches' — required a second implementation pass
The matchedSignal type, AllowsSingleton logic, and AffectedSessionSet method were load-bearing but undefined in the doc sketch — had to design them during implementation
open_items: MEMORY_QUALITY_ANALYSIS.md notes that repo_learning and workflow_learning should be removed from the generator prompt or marked context-only to avoid wasted LLM tokens on ineligible signal types
findSignal lookup strategy uses normalized exact match with substring fallback — false negative rate if LLM paraphrases the signal key is not yet measured
Existing low-quality memories already in memory-loop.json are not retroactively filtered; natural decay or a backfill/re-evaluation pass may be needed
GenerationStats now has FilteredNoEvidenceCount but no separate counter to distinguish 'no source_signal field' from 'signal found but count too low'
The improve/generator.go JSON fix was applied but not explicitly tested for the trailing-text case
